minutes.headline: Commission voted to submit a November warrant article directing the select board to sell the Brooks house.
minutes.summary: The Architectural Preservation District Commission approved prior minutes, heard the chair's report on talks with the town manager about funding Ritter and Town Hall exterior repairs with ARPA money, and discussed the municipal building design committee's hybrid plan. The main action was a motion, apparently approved by voice, to put a Brooks house sale article on the November special town meeting warrant as a placeholder. Members also discussed a possible merger with the Historical Commission, 763 Mass Ave, and a property-owner mailing.

what_happened.line: The commission voted by voice, with no count and no opposition heard, to submit a Brooks house article to the November town meeting warrant directing the select board toward a sale.
Members agreed to leave a deed restriction out of the Brooks house article so it stays simple, and split up outreach to the select board, planning board and Historical Commission.
A warrant article on 763 Mass Ave and extending the district was left off the November warrant; planning board talks are to start later, aiming for May.
The 8 August minutes could not be approved because of a computer problem and were deferred to October; the 10 October meeting will be Zoom only.
The chair reported that the town manager's priority is having ARPA money under signed contract by year end, and members were asked to send repair priorities for Ritter and Town Hall.

why_it_matters: If the Brooks house article reaches the warrant, residents at the November special town meeting would be asked to vote on directing the select board to take steps toward selling a town-held historic property.

ARPA money has a year-end contracting deadline, so whether it goes to preliminary design of a municipal building or to already-designed repairs such as Ritter and Town Hall exteriors is being decided against that clock.
watch_next: Chair meets town counsel on 25 September about a possible Historical Commission and APDC merger; members may attend.
The 10 October meeting (Zoom only) is where the 8 August minutes are expected to be approved.
